author: human
request:
Feature request: filter the vet list by specialty. Three product decisions
come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of
  scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in.
  Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The JSON endpoint at /vets is reinstated as a supported surface — this
  filter is its first requested capability. Mint a fresh requirement for it;
  the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused.
- The filter is a URL contract only. Neither surface gains a form, dropdown,
  or other page control in this request; pagination links carry the
  parameter so filtered pages stay navigable. A visible control may come as
  a follow-up request.

Both vet list surfaces accept an optional `specialty` query parameter:

- /vets.html?specialty=<name> — the HTML page shows only vets holding that
  specialty; pagination applies to the filtered list.
- /vets?specialty=<name> — the JSON endpoint returns only those vets.

Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive — not a prefix. A
specialty matching no vet yields the normal page or JSON document with an
empty vet list (HTTP 200). An empty or whitespace-only value behaves as if
the parameter were absent, like the empty owner search. Without the parameter
both endpoints behave as today. Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can narrow the veterinarian list to one specialty
summary: Both the veterinarian directory page and the machine-readable veterinarian list can be narrowed to the veterinarians holding one named specialty, matched on the whole name regardless of letter case. A blank or absent specialty leaves both unchanged; paging keeps the narrowing. The narrowing is an address contract only, with no page control.
acceptance_criteria: [REQ-VET-003] /vets.html?specialty=<name> lists only the veterinarians holding that specialty; the page count and each page's contents come from the narrowed list, not the full one.
[REQ-VET-003] /vets?specialty=<name> returns only the veterinarians holding that specialty in the machine-readable document.
[REQ-VET-003] matching is on the whole specialty name, disregarding letter case, on both surfaces: 'SURGERY' and 'Surgery' match surgery; 'surg' matches no veterinarian (not a prefix).

[REQ-VET-003] a specialty no veterinarian holds, including a name that is no specialty at all, yields the normal page or document with an empty veterinarian list and a success status (HTTP 200), not a failure.
[REQ-VET-003] an empty or whitespace-only specialty behaves exactly as if the parameter were absent, on both surfaces.
[REQ-VET-003] on a narrowed directory page, every pagination link (each page number, first, previous, next, last) carries the specialty, so following it keeps the list narrowed.
[REQ-VET-003] a matching veterinarian who holds several specialties appears once in the narrowed list and is shown with every specialty they hold, not only the matched one.
[REQ-VET-001][REQ-VET-004] without the parameter both surfaces behave as today: the page lists every veterinarian a page at a time, and the document returns every veterinarian with their specialties.
non_goals: Any form, dropdown, or other page control for choosing a specialty, on either surface (owner: a visible control may come as a follow-up request).
Indicating on the page which specialty is active.
Free-text, partial-name, or prefix veterinarian search (NG-9, narrowed).
Narrowing by more than one specialty at once, or by any attribute other than specialty.
Paging the machine-readable list, or any other change to either surface's behavior when no specialty is named.
notes: ID choice (reversible before commit): REQ-VET-003 is the specialty filter, matching the intake's req_id. The owner's fresh requirement for the reinstated machine-readable list is REQ-VET-004, and today's behavior already meets it. REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn; the Superseded entry now names REQ-VET-004 as its successor. The NG-9 narrowing is recorded in docs/adr/2026-09-12-non-goal-veterinarian-search-narrowed.md. Its docs/adr/README.md index row is outside the PRD write scope, so the design stage or root must add it. docs/system-design.md is stale against this slice: the Overview says there is no JSON API; the Known Defects row says the machine-readable route serves no requirement; the Vets/VetController Implements cells and the Outputs line need updating. The design stage records the owner's address contract there: an optional 'specialty' query parameter on /vets.html and /vets. Open questions, recorded in docs/prd.md and left open (no requirement, no binding test): a visible control or active-specialty indication; whether attribute filtering reaches the veterinarian's name; specialty values with surrounding spaces, or a repeated specialty parameter. Narrowest reading taken: a single specialty per request, a whole-name case-insensitive match on the value as given, and the blank case handled only as stated.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Existing vet feature package, unchanged shape: VetController delegates straight to VetRepository (system-design.md § Overview, feature-package organization without a service layer), mirroring the owner search's paged derived query (OwnerRepository.findByLastNameStartingWith, located by grep at OwnerRepository.java:45; no IDE oracle connected, so grep is the weaker basis). The adjustment: VetRepository gains the specialty-narrowed reads, paged for the directory page and unpaged for the machine-readable list, and both vet routes accept the optional specialty query parameter. The whole-name, case-insensitive match lives in the repository query, not the controller (architecture-principles.md § Pattern Catalog, Web controller row). The controller only normalizes a blank value to absent, which that row classes as binding. The machine-readable route is reinstated as a supported surface (REQ-VET-004); today's code already meets it, so the change is documentation plus the narrowing. No new module, pattern, dependency, or ADR: the uncached narrowed reads are a choice this slice contains. Design-doc writes: system-design.md (provenance banner exception sentence; Overview machine-readable surface; Contracts rows Vet, Specialty, Vets, VetRepository, VetController, CacheConfiguration now cite REQ-VET-003/REQ-VET-004; Persistence paragraph on query-side case folding; Known Defects row for the unconsumed machine-readable route removed; Security Context inputs/outputs; Threat Model SQL-injection and XSS rows extended, new cache-key exhaustion row) and docs/adr/README.md (index row for the product expert's 2026-09-12 NG-9 non-goal ADR).
integration_points: Binding, GET /vets.html: optional `specialty` bound as a request-scoped String next to the existing int `page`. No persisted or form type is bound, so no identifier disallow-list applies (security-principles.md § Realization, mass-assignment row).
Binding, GET /vets: the same optional request-scoped String `specialty`. The Vets wrapper stays the response root.

Controller normalization (architecture-principles.md § Pattern Catalog, Web controller row): a null, empty, or whitespace-only value takes exactly today's unfiltered calls. A non-blank value goes to the repository as given, unstripped, per the prd-entry's narrowest reading.

VetRepository: two new reads, veterinarians holding the named specialty, paged (Pageable -> Page<Vet>) and unpaged (Collection<Vet>). Use Spring Data derived queries with IgnoreCase and Distinct, marked @Transactional(readOnly = true) like their siblings and with no @Cacheable (system-design.md § Contracts, VetRepository row). Derived queries keep the Threat Model SQL-injection mitigation true as written.
Directory page model: the controller exposes the normalized specialty (absent when blank) beside currentPage/totalPages. totalPages and totalItems come from the narrowed Page.

vetList.html: every pagination link (page numbers, first, previous, next, last) is built with Thymeleaf link-expression parameters. The specialty is included only when narrowed, so unnarrowed hrefs render as they do today.
Double, framework transport: MockMvc, the sanctioned transport stand-in (testing-principles.md § Mocking Policy).

Double, repository boundary: the real VetRepository on the embedded H2 database with its seed data. A stub cannot exercise whole-name, case-insensitive, distinct matching, so a framework stub does not fit any binding test here. VetControllerTests moves from @WebMvcTest plus @MockitoBean to a full application context with MockMvc. The two existing tests hold on seed data (vet id 1 is James Carter) and are renamed to the BDD form because the slice touches them. The Mockito stub and its fixtures retire. Seed coverage: surgery is held by vets 3 and 4, and vet 3 also holds dentistry (the several-specialties case); 'surg' and an unknown name give the empty case.

Multi-page narrowed case (links carry the specialty, page count from the narrowed list): the test persists extra veterinarians holding one specialty through the JPA EntityManager inside its own rolled-back @Transactional test, and requests only narrowed surfaces. MockMvc runs on the test thread, so the controller sees the uncommitted rows.

patterns.description: paged derived-query read over a caller-supplied value; the narrowed vet reads follow this shape
existing findPaginated/addPaginationModel helpers; the narrowed path reuses the same page size and model attributes
@Transactional(readOnly = true) on each read; @Cacheable stays only on the two unfiltered reads

risks.risk: Relying on column collation for case-insensitivity: H2 VARCHAR and PostgreSQL TEXT specialty names are case-sensitive, MySQL is not, so results would differ by vendor.
risks.mitigation: Fold case in the query (IgnoreCase), per system-design.md § Persistence, the specialty-narrowed paragraph. Known Defects row 1 (PostgreSQL owner search) is the precedent this avoids.

risks.risk: A fetch join on specialties in the narrowed query would load only the matched specialty and page in memory, breaking PRD edge case 2 (each veterinarian shown with every specialty).
risks.mitigation: Join only to select, and let Vet's own eager mapping load the specialties (system-design.md § Persistence). The vet-3 surgery+dentistry assertion guards it.

risks.risk: The join duplicates a veterinarian holding the specialty twice over, or inflates the page count.
risks.mitigation: Distinct on both reads, so the derived count counts distinct veterinarians (system-design.md § Contracts, VetRepository row: 'return each veterinarian once').

risks.risk: Following the siblings and adding @Cacheable to the narrowed reads makes each caller-chosen name a new unbounded vet-cache entry.
risks.mitigation: No @Cacheable on the narrowed reads (system-design.md § Threat Model, cache-key exhaustion row; Contracts VetRepository row).

risks.risk: Building links by string concatenation or __${...}__ preprocessing with the request-derived specialty opens expression injection and unencoded markup in href.
risks.mitigation: Use link-expression parameters, as in @{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})} when narrowed. Never put the specialty in preprocessing or a concatenated URL (security-principles.md § Realization, injection and XSS rows; system-design.md § Threat Model, XSS row).

risks.risk: Unnarrowed pagination hrefs gain a bare or empty specialty parameter, changing today's page (REQ-VET-001 'behave as today').
risks.mitigation: Render the specialty parameter only when a normalized specialty is present (system-design.md § Contracts, VetController row: 'a blank value counts as absent').

risks.risk: The matching rule drifts into the controller, for example by filtering findAll() in memory.
risks.mitigation: The controller only normalizes blank to absent. Matching stays in the repository query (architecture-principles.md § Pattern Catalog, Web controller row and the paragraph after it).

risks.risk: A full-context test that requests an unfiltered surface after inserting rolled-back vets leaves those rows in the live vet cache for later tests.
risks.mitigation: Tests that insert request only narrowed, uncached surfaces (system-design.md § Contracts, VetRepository row: unfiltered reads are cached).

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log; skipped. Paging order: neither paged read orders its results (pre-existing), so the narrowed page tests should assert page count and membership, not order. Open questions carried without a binding test, following the prd-entry's narrowest reading: surrounding spaces are not stripped. A repeated specialty parameter binds as Spring's comma-joined String, matches no specialty, and yields an empty 200. Owner search strips its value, and the PRD Open Questions entry keeps that asymmetry open. Pre-existing gap recorded, not fixed: the unfiltered paged read is cached per caller-chosen page number and the vet cache has no size bound (new Threat Model row, 'None observed'). Brief defect for the security-principles.md owner, outside this agent's write scope: § Realization has no row for resource exhaustion through caller-chosen keys, so reviewers have no brief line for the cache rule beyond system-design.md § Threat Model. Harness-prose tension: the system-design-expert definition allows 'one clause' of rationale on a current-state line, while design-validation's pre-handoff self-check bars any causal clause. This dispatch followed the stricter form. Non-goal ADR docs/adr/2026-09-12-non-goal-veterinarian-search-narrowed.md was authored by product-requirements-expert and is not claimed here. Only its README index row was written.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Injection into data access: the request-supplied specialty reaches the database only through Spring Data derived queries (VetRepository.java: `Collection<Vet> findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String specialtyName)` and its Pageable overload). These are bound parameters with no string-concatenated query text, which matches the security-principles.md injection control.

Cross-site scripting / output escaping: the specialty is echoed only in the pagination links, as a link-expression parameter (vetList.html:32 `@{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}`, and lines 38/44/50/56 likewise). Thymeleaf URL-encodes the value and attribute-escapes the th:href output. The path stays fixed, so no javascript:/data: scheme can be injected. A grep for `th:utext` across src/main/ found nothing, and VetControllerTests round-trips the value 'ear, nose & throat' through the links.

Template-expression evaluation: the change removes the `__${...}__` preprocessing from every vetList.html pagination link. `grep -rn -F '__${' src/main/` now lists only owner/layout fragments that the change did not touch, all over server-side values. No request-supplied text enters preprocessing.

Resource exhaustion via caller-chosen cache keys: the new narrowed reads carry only `@Transactional(readOnly = true)` and no `@Cacheable`. VetRepository.java:45/55 shows `@Cacheable("vets")` only on the two pre-existing findAll methods. So a caller cannot grow the unbounded 'vets' cache (CacheConfiguration.java:37) with arbitrary specialty names. The page-number keying that remains was already there and is recorded in system-design.md's threat model.

Exposed surface: no new route. The optional `specialty` parameter narrows the existing /vets.html and /vets responses to a subset of data those routes already return. No request binding target (@ModelAttribute/@RequestBody) is added, so mass assignment does not apply.

Blank or absent specialty handling fails safe to the unfiltered read (`StringUtils.hasText`). A non-matching or over-long name produces an empty list, not an error, so no exception message carrying the value reaches the error page.
No secrets, logging, file I/O, shell execution, or deserialization in the diff. A grep for `JsonTypeInfo`/`enableDefaultTyping` in src/main/ found nothing.

Supply chain: the change set has no build files (`git status --short -- build.gradle settings.gradle gradle/` is empty). `./gradlew dependencies --configuration runtimeClasspath` resolves Spring Boot 4.1.1 (spring-boot-thymeleaf), jackson-databind 3.1.5, Thymeleaf 3.1.5.RELEASE and Hibernate 7.4.5.Final. No NVD match was run, because dependencyCheckAnalyze is not configured and this review has no network access.

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: `PAGE_SIZE` was widened from a private local variable in `findPaginated` to a package-private static field solely so `VetControllerTests` can read `VetController.PAGE_SIZE` (the only other reference, at VetControllerTests.java:123,125). This is the placement smell the code-quality-review skill names directly: a helper widened for test access instead of testing through the sanctioned seam.
findings.fix: Revert `PAGE_SIZE` to a private (or local) constant in `VetController`, and give `VetControllerTests` its own local constant for the expected page size (e.g. a private `PAGE_SIZE = 5`) instead of reaching into `VetController.PAGE_SIZE`.

findings.description: The `${specialty == null} ? @{...} : @{...}` conditional is repeated identically at all five pagination-link sites added by this diff (the page-number loop plus first/previous/next/last), each differing only in the page value. Confirmed necessary in principle — Thymeleaf renders a null `@{}` parameter as a bare `specialty=` rather than omitting it (thymeleaf/thymeleaf#846), which is why the ternary exists — but its boolean condition is duplicated across all five sibling sites rather than computed once, the exact case the code-quality-review checklist's Control Flow section calls out.
findings.fix: Compute the condition once with `th:with="narrowed=${specialty != null}"` on the enclosing `<div th:if="${totalPages > 1}">` and reference `${narrowed}` at each of the five link sites instead of repeating `${specialty == null}` inline.

author: change-grader
summary: narrow the vet list surfaces by an optional specialty parameter

blast_radius.note: Contained to the vet feature package: two optional request parameters in VetController, two uncached derived reads in VetRepository, the pagination block of vetList.html, and the slice's own docs. No sensitive paths. The two security-surface files carry a new caller-supplied value, but it reaches SQL only as a bound derived-query parameter and HTML only as a URL-encoded link-expression parameter. The 52 hunks sit mostly in the test rewrite and the docs.

semantic_surprise.note: Read every prod hunk. The blank check (StringUtils.hasText) gates both the query choice and the model attribute. The derived query is an upper-equality match, so it covers the whole name and never acts as a prefix. Distinct also applies to the page count. The fix-round th:with keeps the right polarity (narrowed = specialty != null selects the specialty-bearing link). The unnarrowed hrefs switch from __${}__ preprocessing to link expressions but render the same, and a test pins that. The known asymmetries are recorded as PRD open questions, not hidden: surrounding spaces are not stripped, and a repeated parameter binds comma-joined.

test_adequacy.note: The tests drive the real repository on seeded H2 through MockMvc. They assert outcomes: case variants, a prefix that must miss, empty and unknown names, blank and whitespace pages byte-identical to absent, narrowed totalPages and totalItems over persisted rows, links round-tripping 'ear, nose & throat', and unnarrowed links unchanged. One small gap: containsOnlyOnce(DOUGLAS) cannot tell whether Distinct is present, because duplicates would need case-variant specialty rows that no app path creates.
